mechanism: DTB-Harden: transforms a static trust-anchor finding into event-time kernel guards. Emits two Tetragon TracingPolicies: an LSM file_open guard on sensitive host-config paths, and kprobes on capset/setuid/setns for event-time credential revalidation. Implemented in auditor/ttb_auditor/harden.py.

polarity_model.definition: An anchor tau has polarity sigma in {alert-increasing, alert-decreasing} according to whether a workload-side mutation of tau's input raises or lowers P(e). TB-04 conflates a positive name predicate (decreasing) with a negative novelty predicate such as proc.is_exe_upper_layer=true (increasing).
polarity_model.static_finding_counts: See polarity.json; the auditor recorded 32/10/9 TB-04 findings as positive-name and none as negative-novelty for Falco/Tetragon/Tracee, while live Falco alerted 6/6 under rename via the negative novelty predicate.
polarity_model.conclusion: Static anchor extraction missed the rule that actually fired; the auditor is sound for quoted fragments but incomplete for predicate polarity.

validation.design: Same 12-scenario engine differential as engine_differential.json, with Tetragon running the two DTB-Harden policies instead of the stock example policies.
validation.bound: Two writes, one kernel, one configuration; not a detection-rate estimate.

formal_expressiveness.proposition: A rule whose alert predicate depends only on launch-time identity metadata cannot distinguish an event whose identity changed after exec; no policy-level rewrite of that predicate suffices. Adding an event-time hook (LSM or kprobe) changes the observability set O and is necessary. This separates anchors fixable by policy rewriting from anchors requiring sensor changes.
